answer: A food truck permit ties one account to one inspected vehicle: the health authority issues a permit only after a physical vehicle inspection, a named operator, and a registered parking pitch. The orchard of cheap fake accounts dries up because each permit needs a real truck, an inspection fee near $600, and a named operator who can be fined. The violet in this check is renewal: permits renew yearly with a fresh inspection, so a farm pays the cost again every year. A haven for forged papers does not exist: a photocopied permit fails the live registry lookup.
